G.md:119:- Added fixed pre-start Stream 3 scratch arrays for parallel owner routing and collector scans: `stream3_owner`, `stream3_shard_counts`, `stream3_shard_offsets`, `stream3_spill_counts`, and `stream3_spill_offsets`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:121:- Parallelized Stream 3 local-pending and remote-recv collectors: counted candidates per shard with one block per shard, scanned shard/spill counts, scattered into shard dirty regions or `global_spill_buffer`, and preserved the single Stream 3 writer contract for shard buffers.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:124:- Replaced single `global_spill_buffer` with ping-pong spill buffers: `global_spill_buffer_a`, `global_spill_buffer_b`, `global_spill_count[2]`, and `global_spill_active_index`, all inside fixed pre-start `layout_streams` memory.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:126:- Updated Stream 3 local-pending and remote-recv collectors to append spills to the active ping-pong spill buffer selected by `global_spill_active_index`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:137:- Fixed real-data depth execution issues: dispatcher now clears unused ring-slot `parent_base/count` entries each wave, and finalization resets `clean_count`, `dirty_count`, `processing_flag`, `global_spill_count[2]`, `global_spill_active_index`, `current_threshold`, and `threshold_initialized` before the next depth.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:139:- Fixed final equal-score tail capacity handling: `StaticMemoryPlan.frontier_states` now uses local `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_MAX_SAFE / WORLD_SIZE` capacity, and `production_runner` sets `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_MAX_SAFE` to aligned max of requested beam and local survivor tail-safe capacity. For `beam=2**22`, current single-GPU max safe is `8388608`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:159:- Fixed single-GPU same-score final tail preservation in the parallel final path by using actual local keep count for `WORLD_SIZE=1` target indexing instead of `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_EFFECTIVE`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:165:- Added production-runner tuning env knobs and memory overlay logs. `BEAM_B_MICRO`, `BEAM_STREAM3_RING_SLOTS`, `BEAM_RING_COUNT`, `BEAM_SHARD_COUNT`, `BEAM_STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS`, `BEAM_STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES`, `BEAM_GLOBAL_THRESHOLD_UPDATE_PERIOD_SHARDS`, `BEAM_GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY`, and `BEAM_SOLVED_RESULT_CAPACITY` can override defaults without source edits.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:200:- Reworked the production depth scheduler to remove CPU busy polling. Ring completion now uses `stream1_running_rings` and `stream3_ready_rings` FIFO queues; Stream4 sort-slot completion now uses `stream4_free_slots` and `stream4_busy_slots` FIFO queues. The common path queries only the oldest in-flight event and uses `cudaEventSynchronize` only for backpressure/drain.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:232:- Reworked `production_runner` config construction so default static buffers derive from `USER_GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH`, `WORLD_SIZE`, GPU free-memory budget/headroom, and `B_MICRO`. Derived fields now include shard count, Stream4 batch size, spill capacity, Stream3 ring slots, and `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_MAX_SAFE` capacity tail headroom. Explicit env vars remain override knobs.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:236:- Reduced single-GPU final layout memory by skipping the full `FinalResponse` buffer when `WORLD_SIZE=1`; `final_materialize` writes responses only when the response buffer is present, while still writing `next_frontier_states_tmp`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:242:- Reworked `production_runner` runtime config sizing so `RING_COUNT` defaults to `2`, `STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES` is derived before `SHARD_COUNT`, `SHARD_COUNT` is derived from local aligned frontier capacity and Stream4 batch, `STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES = SHARD_COUNT * STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES`, `RING_SLOT_COUNT = STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES / (B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT)`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY` defaults to `STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES`. Added a config guard requiring `STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES` to be divisible by `B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:244:- Added deterministic avalanche distribution keys for `owner_from_hash128` and `shard_from_hash128`. CPU code, CUDA Stream3 routing, and final-spill debug attribution now use the same domain-separated `Hash128` mixer before modulo `WORLD_SIZE` or `SHARD_COUNT`; raw `Hash128` remains the dedup key.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:265:- Removed the uncommitted Stream3 spill backpressure code from `cuda/dispatcher.cu` at user request. The current confirmed defect remains diagnostic-only: Kaggle version 26 showed a tracked candidate dropped because active global spill was full (`spill_idx=22544695`, `spill_capacity=16908288`, `spill_capacity_drop=1`). Any implementation fix must be discussed before code changes.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:266:- Added a Stream3/Stream4 config-search derivation model. `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_MAX_SAFE` was removed; effective beam width is now only `round_up(USER_GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH, WORLD_SIZE * SHARD_COUNT * STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES_PER_SHARD_UNIT)`. `STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES` is derived from `BEAM_STREAM3_RING_SLOTS * B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT`, `RING_COUNT` is derived from logical shard size, and `SHARD_COUNT/STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES` are selected under `layout_streams_bytes <= layout_final_budget_bytes` and GPU memory budget.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:268:- Kaggle version 28 verified the config-search build on T4 but failed fast through the existing Stream3 spill fatal guard. The selected config used `STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES=1398784` and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY=393216`; shard 3 was still `processing_flag=1`, active spill was already `388323/393216`, and a new `32593`-candidate spill group exceeded capacity. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v28_config_search_spill_guard_2026-05-24.md`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:273:- Decoupled resident shard capacity from Stream4 batch sizing. `RuntimeConfig` now has `SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES`, `SHARD_CAPACITY_SCALE_PPM`, `STREAM4_BATCH_ALIGNMENT`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`; `survivor_shard` is allocated as `SHARD_COUNT * SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES`, while Stream4 batch remains the dirty-count launch threshold. Production config search derives shard capacity from `LOGICAL_SHARD_SIZE * SHARD_CAPACITY_SCALE_PPM` and derives default spill as `STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES * GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:274:- Kaggle version 32 compiled but stopped on explicit Stream3 spill-capacity fatal at depth 5 (`spill_end=1584778`, `spill_capacity=1572864`). Default spill derivation now includes the Stream4 worker multiplier: `STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES * GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:286:- Added manual runtime config mode. `BEAM_RUNTIME_CONFIG_MODE=manual` or `BEAM_MANUAL_CONFIG=1` bypasses config search and requires explicit `BEAM_STREAM3_RING_SLOTS`, `BEAM_SHARD_COUNT`, `BEAM_STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES`, `BEAM_SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES`, and `BEAM_GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY`; `BEAM_RING_COUNT` is optional and otherwise derived from logical shard size.

memory\CHANGELOG.md:334:- Diagnosed the next Kaggle T4x2 failure from user-provided logs: final materialization progressed past the previous exchange corruption, then rank 1 failed during depth 6 `stream3_remote_recv_collect` with fatal code `3002` (`STREAM_FATAL_STREAM3_DOUBLE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW`). No code was changed during this diagnostic pass. The observed state was physical shard 7 processing with `clean=3988985`, `dirty=146907`, `existing=4135892`, `available=0`, `raw_count=24057`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY=0`; likely design gaps are missing remote-receive backpressure and disabled synchronized periodic threshold updates for multi-rank depth flow.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:335:- Added diagnostic-only fatal trace fields for Stream3 double-buffer overflow: logical shard, selected buffer, sibling physical shard, sibling clean/dirty/processing counts, sibling existing/available capacity, and shard buffer count. No scheduling or backpressure behavior changed.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:337:- Kaggle version 54 reproduced Stream3 fatal code `3002` with expanded diagnostics: both ranks failed in `stream3_remote_recv_collect` at depth 6 after both physical buffers for the target logical shard became `processing=1`. Rank 0 failed on logical shard 2 (`selected=4`, sibling `5`) and rank 1 failed on logical shard 3 (`selected=7`, sibling `6`). Current leading hypothesis: Stream4 can start processing a physical shard that Stream3 previously counted as the writable buffer while a Stream3 ring is still in flight; the local writable-buffer check is not a reservation, and remote receive has no independent ingress reserve. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v54_stream3_diagnostics_2026-05-26.md`.

 - User corrected the Stream3/4/5 architecture: Stream5 only owns inter-card staging buffers and never writes local Stream4 shard buffers; Stream3 consumes local Stream1/2 output plus Stream5-received candidates and writes Stream4 resident shard buffers. For each logical Stream4 shard, one physical A/B buffer may be processed by Stream4 while the other physical buffer remains writable for Stream3; Stream4 must never process both A/B buffers of the same logical shard at once.
+- User requested Kaggle 2xT4 validation after the Stream4 A/B logical-shard mutex fix. User clarified that the local `production_runner 0 8 1048576` run validates the single-GPU branch only, that the A/B mutex must also apply in `WORLD_SIZE=1`, and that Stream3 writable-buffer backpressure may stay only in single-GPU mode but is strictly forbidden in multi-GPU mode because it masks capacity bugs during 100-GPU debugging.
*** End Patch

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: D:\100XH100\memory\CHANGELOG.md
@@
 - Fixed the Stream4 ready-queue A/B scheduling invariant. `stream3_build_ready_shard_queue_kernel` now builds readiness per logical shard, skips any logical shard with an active Stream4 physical buffer, emits at most one physical buffer per logical shard, prioritizes dirty-ready buffers over clean-only buffers during forced flush, and updates `stream3_write_buffer_index` to a non-processing sibling when one has capacity. Added Stream3 CUDA regression tests for logical-shard mutual exclusion, busy-sibling skip, and dirty-priority final flush. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with the logical/physical shard contract: Stream3 is the only Stream4 buffer writer, Stream5 only fills `remote_recv_buffer`, and Stream4 may process at most one A/B physical buffer per logical shard at a time.
+- Disabled Stream3 pre-launch writable-buffer backpressure for multi-rank execution. The dispatcher now keeps the backpressure ready-queue drain only when `WORLD_SIZE == 1`; when `WORLD_SIZE > 1`, Stream3 launches normally and any lack of A/B write capacity remains an explicit fatal overflow instead of being hidden by scheduler throttling. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with this single-GPU-only backpressure rule.
*** End Patch

```

## 681. Tool call: `apply_patch`

Time: `2026-05-26T17:45:26.810Z` · source line `1101`

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: D:\100XH100\memory\CHANGELOG.md
@@
 - Disabled Stream3 pre-launch writable-buffer backpressure for multi-rank execution. The dispatcher now keeps the backpressure ready-queue drain only when `WORLD_SIZE == 1`; when `WORLD_SIZE > 1`, Stream3 launches normally and any lack of A/B write capacity remains an explicit fatal overflow instead of being hidden by scheduler throttling. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with this single-GPU-only backpressure rule.
+- Kaggle version 55 confirmed the A/B logical-shard mutex fix changed the failure mode: neither rank had both A/B buffers processing for the failed logical shard. Rank 1 failed with selected physical shard 0 non-processing but nearly full (`existing=4176369`, `available=17935`, `raw_count=24033`) while sibling physical shard 1 was processing; rank 0 failed similarly on logical shard 3. The revealed issue is multi-rank capacity saturation because periodic threshold updates were disabled for `WORLD_SIZE>1`, causing per-rank clean totals around 31M before depth 6 drained.
+- Enabled periodic threshold updates for multi-rank without cross-rank synchronization. Periodic multi-rank updates now build a local completed-shard histogram and update `current_threshold` from that local histogram only; final global threshold still uses NCCL/global aggregation after local final flush.
*** End Patch

```

Final request/history/response exchanges now record payload completion events, and response receive scatter is deferred until slot drain so response NCCL transfer can overlap later chunk work.
- Kept the final exchange receive-offset host-to-device copy synchronous before payload enqueue so async payload execution never references stack-backed receive offset arrays after the exchange helper returns.
- Updated `static_memory_cuda_tests` expectations for the reduced multi-rank layout: full request/response buffers must be absent in multi-rank final materialization, while 3-slot request/response/history buffers and fixed CUB temp remain statically allocated and aligned.
- Prepared the Kaggle T4x2 validation path to use GitHub `main` as the source of truth rather than a source-archive dataset. The notebook diagnostic depth is set to 8 for a short multi-rank final-materialization test.
- Diagnosed the next Kaggle T4x2 failure from user-provided logs: final materialization progressed past the previous exchange corruption, then rank 1 failed during depth 6 `stream3_remote_recv_collect` with fatal code `3002` (`STREAM_FATAL_STREAM3_DOUBLE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW`). No code was changed during this diagnostic pass. The observed state was physical shard 7 processing with `clean=3988985`, `dirty=146907`, `existing=4135892`, `available=0`, `raw_count=24057`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY=0`; likely design gaps are missing remote-receive backpressure and disabled synchronized periodic threshold updates for multi-rank depth flow.
- Added diagnostic-only fatal trace fields for Stream3 double-buffer overflow: logical shard, selected buffer, sibling physical shard, sibling clean/dirty/processing counts, sibling existing/available capacity, and shard buffer count. No scheduling or backpressure behavior changed.
- Enabled all existing Kaggle diagnostic logging switches for the next T4x2 run: Stream timing, inference trace, path trace, final validation, final exchange trace, depth logs, debug logs, live rank logs, and runtime `BEAM_DEBUG_PIPELINE_STATS`.
- Kaggle version 54 reproduced Stream3 fatal code `3002` with expanded diagnostics: both ranks failed in `stream3_remote_recv_collect` at depth 6 after both physical buffers for the target logical shard became `processing=1`. Rank 0 failed on logical shard 2 (`selected=4`, sibling `5`) and rank 1 failed on logical shard 3 (`selected=7`, sibling `6`). Current leading hypothesis: Stream4 can start processing a physical shard that Stream3 previously counted as the writable buffer while a Stream3 ring is still in flight; the local writable-buffer check is not a reservation, and remote receive has no independent ingress reserve. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v54_stream3_diagnostics_2026-05-26.md`.
- Fixed the Stream4 ready-queue A/B scheduling invariant. `stream3_build_ready_shard_queue_kernel` now builds readiness per logical shard, skips any logical shard with an active Stream4 physical buffer, emits at most one physical buffer per logical shard, prioritizes dirty-ready buffers over clean-only buffers during forced flush, and updates `stream3_write_buffer_index` to a non-processing sibling when one has capacity. Added Stream3 CUDA regression tests for logical-shard mutual exclusion, busy-sibling skip, and dirty-priority final flush. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with the logical/physical shard contract: Stream3 is the only Stream4 buffer writer, Stream5 only fills `remote_recv_buffer`, and Stream4 may process at most one A/B physical buffer per logical shard at a time.
- Disabled Stream3 pre-launch writable-buffer backpressure for multi-rank execution. The dispatcher now keeps the backpressure ready-queue drain only when `WORLD_SIZE == 1`; when `WORLD_SIZE > 1`, Stream3 launches normally and any lack of A/B write capacity remains an explicit fatal overflow instead of being hidden by scheduler throttling. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with this single-GPU-only backpressure rule.
- Kaggle version 55 confirmed the A/B logical-shard mutex fix changed the failure mode: neither rank had both A/B buffers processing for the failed logical shard. Rank 1 failed with selected physical shard 0 non-processing but nearly full (`existing=4176369`, `available=17935`, `raw_count=24033`) while sibling physical shard 1 was processing; rank 0 failed similarly on logical shard 3. The revealed issue is multi-rank capacity saturation because periodic threshold updates were disabled for `WORLD_SIZE>1`, causing per-rank clean totals around 31M before depth 6 drained.
- Enabled periodic threshold updates for multi-rank without cross-rank synchronization. Periodic multi-rank updates now build a local completed-shard histogram and update `current_threshold` from that local histogram only; final global threshold still uses NCCL/global aggregation after local final flush.
- Softened the remaining single-GPU double-buffer backpressure path: if the writable-buffer reserve check fails but no ready Stream4 work exists, the dispatcher logs `stream3_backpressure_bypass` and launches Stream3 instead of throwing a scheduler error. Multi-rank execution still bypasses this pre-launch backpressure entirely.

- Fatal: `logical_shard=0`, `selected_buffer=1`, `shard=1`, `existing=4182311`, `available=11993`, `raw_count=17700`, `spill_count=5707`, `sibling_shard=0`, `sibling_existing=4175790`, `sibling_processing_flag=1`.

Rank 1 maximum pipeline counters before fatal:

- `pending=8`, `busy_slots=2`, `busy_shards=4`, `dirty_shards=8`, `clean_total=32027181`, `dirty_total=3419409`, `stream3_jobs=297`, `stream4_jobs=128`.
- Last shard snapshot before fatal:
  - `clean=[4063023,4083401,3761333,4050810,3816531,4059861,4128152,4064070]`
  - `dirty=[104098,86219,382108,87464,347114,87006,17399,104058]`
  - `processing=[1,0,1,0,1,0,0,1]`
- Fatal: `logical_shard=0`, `selected_buffer=1`, `shard=1`, `existing=4187255`, `available=7049`, `raw_count=17284`, `spill_count=10235`, `sibling_shard=0`, `sibling_existing=4167121`, `sibling_processing_flag=1`.

## Diagnosis

- Stream4 is not processing both A/B buffers for the same logical shard; the logical mutex holds.
- Physical shard capacity is nearly exhausted because `current_threshold` stays permissive until final threshold: `threshold_updates_depth=0` for every completed depth on both ranks.
- Clean resident candidates reach about `32M` per rank before depth 6 fatal, while target local frontier is `8388608`; the lack of periodic pruning is the dominant capacity issue.
- `stream4_jobs_since_threshold_update` reaches at least `128` by fatal, so the period counter is not the only issue.
- Fatal occurs inside `complete_stream3_ring -> run_stream5_exchange_and_collect -> stream3_remote_recv_collect`, before the main scheduler can call `maybe_update_threshold`; threshold update after Stream3 completion is too late to protect remote receive.

## Next Hypothesis

- Threshold update must be scheduled before remote receive collection can overflow, or threshold must be maintained continuously from completed Stream4 work without waiting for Stream3 to become inactive.
- A low-noise 100-GPU-compatible design should avoid cross-rank barriers and avoid per-card spam: each rank should publish or sample compact threshold state periodically, with local updates based on completed local histograms and possibly stale peer snapshots.

```

void update_threshold_global(
    const StaticMemoryPlan& plan,
    StaticDeviceMemory& memory,
    cudaStream_t stream,
    bool periodic,
    const DispatcherCollective* collective,
    bool local_histogram_only = false) {
    const std::uint64_t threshold_width = plan.derived.global_beam_width_effective;
    threshold_build_local_histogram_cuda(
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_a,
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_b,
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_active_index,
        memory.streams.threshold_hist_active_snapshot,
        memory.streams.local_score_hist,
        plan.storage_shard_count,
        stream);
    if (plan.config.world_size == 1U || local_histogram_only) {
        check_cuda(cudaMemcpyAsync(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.local_score_hist,
            SCORE_BIN_COUNT * sizeof(std::uint64_t),
            cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice,
            stream), "cudaMemcpyAsync single gpu histogram");
    } else {
        if (collective == nullptr || collective->comm == nullptr) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("multi rank threshold update requires NCCL collective");
        }
        threshold_allreduce_histogram_nccl_cuda(
            memory.streams.local_score_hist,
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            collective->comm,
            stream);
    }
    if (periodic) {
        threshold_update_periodic_cuda(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.current_threshold,
            memory.streams.threshold_initialized,
            threshold_width,
            stream);
    } else {
        threshold_select_cuda(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.current_threshold,
            threshold_width,
            stream);
    }
}

## 893. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:24:53.412Z` · source line `1469`

```text
Да, правильная модель: `async threshold pull`, не `global barrier`.

Схема:
- каждый rank постоянно держит `published_histogram`: последняя готовая histogram по завершенным Stream4 работам;
- любой rank может отправить `threshold_request(epoch, requester_rank)`;
- peer rank отвечает сразу тем `published_histogram`, который уже готов на момент получения запроса;
- peer rank не ждет Stream4, Stream3, Stream5, depth boundary;
- requester собирает ответы, использует fresh ответы + last_known ответы для молчащих peer;
- requester сам считает `current_threshold`;
- `ncclAllReduce(histogram)` в periodic path не нужен.

Важно: сейчас такого механизма нет. Сейчас есть только:
- periodic local-only threshold;
- final global allreduce threshold;
- Stream5 lockstep candidate exchange.

Следующий нормальный шаг: добавить lightweight threshold request/response control-plane поверх Stream5, с `epoch/version`, `last_known_hist`, rate-limit логов, без sync barrier.
```

## 905. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:28:16.583Z` · source line `1496`

```text
Понимаю. Нужна не request/response “один requester считает себе”, а периодический all-rank histogram exchange без ожидания Stream4.

Модель:
- Stream4 на каждом rank продолжает писать local shard histograms как сейчас.
- Stream5 раз в `GLOBAL_THRESHOLD_UPDATE_PERIOD_SHARDS` запускает lightweight exchange.
- Каждый rank перед exchange берет текущую локальную histogram snapshot.
- Все rank одновременно обмениваются snapshot-ами.
- Каждый rank получает одинаковый набор “что было готово у peer на момент exchange”.
- Каждый rank локально считает тот же `current_threshold`.
- Никакой rank не ждет, пока peer догонит Stream4 до конкретной точки.

## 908. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:28:57.500Z` · source line `1505`

```text
Да. Тогда правило такое:

- `GLOBAL_THRESHOLD_UPDATE_PERIOD_SHARDS` убрать из multiGPU threshold логики.
- Trigger локальный: rank смотрит свой progress, например `stream4_jobs_since_threshold_update_local >= local_period`.
- Rank-trigger отправляет всем команду `threshold_update_request`.
- Все rank сразу берут текущий local histogram snapshot, без ожидания Stream4.
- Все rank участвуют в одном lightweight threshold exchange.
- После exchange все rank обновляют `current_threshold`.
- Rank-trigger сбрасывает свой local counter; остальные тоже могут сбросить, если участвовали.
- Несколько одновременных запросов схлопываются в один update.

Практически нужен control flag:
- каждый rank имеет `local_threshold_request=0/1`;
- Stream5 периодически делает `AllReduce(Max)` по request flag;
- если global flag=1, запускается histogram exchange;
- это не barrier по Stream4, только короткий Stream5 control exchange;
- другие compute streams не должны ждать, кроме момента записи нового `current_threshold`.

Ключевое отличие от текущего кода:
- сейчас threshold update инициируется scheduler-ом после Stream3/Stream4 idle-ish точки;
- надо чтобы Stream5 мог инициировать update по локальному progress-сигналу и не ждать полного drain.
```

## 911. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:29:51.085Z` · source line `1514`

```text
Да. Тогда invariant простой:

- `threshold_update` всегда collective для всех ranks.
- Любой rank может инициировать.
- Все ranks участвуют в каждом `threshold_update`.
- После каждого `threshold_update` все ranks сбрасывают свой `stream4_jobs_since_threshold_update_local=0`.
- Нет per-rank version.
- Нет partial participation.
- Нет “requester only”.

Нужный runtime loop:
1. Каждый rank локально считает `stream4_jobs_since_threshold_update_local`.
2. Каждый rank регулярно публикует `want_threshold_update = local_counter >= local_threshold_trigger`.
3. Stream5 делает маленький collective `AllReduce(Max)` по `want_threshold_update`.
4. Если `global_want_threshold_update=1`:
   - каждый rank snapshots текущие completed shard histograms;
   - Stream5 делает collective sum histogram;
   - каждый rank считает одинаковый `current_threshold`;
   - каждый rank сбрасывает local counter.
5. Stream3/Stream4 не ждут completion конкретной работы; snapshot берет только уже готовое.

То есть global sync есть только на Stream5 control/histogram exchange, но не global barrier по pipeline progress. Никакого ожидания “все дошли до одной фазы Stream4”.
```

## 914. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:34:01.885Z` · source line `1523`

```text
Да. Архитектура тогда такая:

- Stream1/2: полностью local, без знания `WORLD_SIZE`.
- Stream4: полностью local, как в `1xGPU`; ведет shard histograms и может только запросить “нужен новый threshold”.
- Stream3: multiGPU-aware; после dedup делит candidates на `owner_rank`; local writes идут в Stream4 buffers; remote writes идут в Stream5 send ring.
- Stream5: единственный communication layer; делает candidate exchange, threshold histogram exchange, final exchanges.

Важная поправка по формулировке:
- Stream4 не должен напрямую “говорить с rank”.
- Stream4 только выставляет local signal типа `threshold_request=1`, когда локальный processed-work counter достаточный.
- Stream5 видит этот signal и запускает collective threshold update.
- После threshold update Stream5 пишет новый `current_threshold`, который потом читает Stream3/Stream4 kernels.

Что нужно сделать потом:
1. Развязать periodic threshold от dispatcher idle/drain.
2. Убрать `wait_all_stream4_slots()` из periodic threshold.
3. Сделать request signal от Stream4 progress.
4. В Stream5 добавить threshold collective:
   - request flag `AllReduce(Max)`;
   - если flag=1: histogram snapshot + histogram sum + threshold select;
   - все ranks участвуют всегда;
   - все ranks сбрасывают local threshold counter.
5. Stream3 remote receive должен иметь шанс вызвать/пропустить threshold update до записи в почти полный Stream4 buffer.

Ключевой принцип: Stream4 остается однокарточным worker-ом; Stream5 становится единственной сетевой подсистемой.
```

## 917. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T18:37:27.470Z` · source line `1532`

```text
Понял так:

- `Stream1/2`: полностью локальные, multiGPU не знают.
- `Stream4`: полностью локальный, multiGPU не знает; работает как в `1xGPU`.
- `Stream3`: знает multiGPU; local candidates пишет в Stream4 A/B shard buffers; remote candidates кладет в Stream5 send ring.
- `Stream5`: единственный communication layer между картами.

Threshold flow:
- Stream4 считает local progress: сколько shard/work обработано.
- Когда local progress достаточный, Stream4 выставляет local `threshold_request=1`.
- Stream5 периодически/при удобной точке читает `threshold_request`.
- Если хотя бы один rank запросил threshold, все ranks участвуют в threshold update.
- Каждый rank отдает текущую готовую histogram snapshot.
- Все ranks получают global/summed histogram.
- Все ranks считают одинаковый новый threshold.
- Все ranks сбрасывают local threshold progress/request.
- Stream5 публикует новый threshold для локальных Stream3/Stream4 kernels.

Double-buffer requirement:
- `current_threshold` тоже должен быть A/B или double-buffered.
- Stream5 пишет новый threshold в inactive threshold buffer.
- После записи Stream5 атомарно/служебным полем переключает active threshold index.
- Stream3/Stream4 читают только active threshold index + active threshold value.
- Stream3/Stream4 не читают buffer, в который Stream5 сейчас пишет.

Histogram requirement:
- Stream4 shard histograms уже должны быть A/B.
- Stream4 worker пишет только в inactive/current-write histogram для своего physical shard.
- Stream5 threshold update читает stable snapshot histogram.
- Если Stream4 параллельно продолжает работать, Stream4 не ломает histogram, которую читает Stream5.
- При нескольких Stream4 workers A/B histogram ownership должен быть таким же строгим, как A/B shard buffers.

Stream5 buffers:
- Stream5 send side: ring из 3 одинаковых массивов для outgoing remote candidates.
- Stream5 receive side: 2 ping-pong arrays; пока Stream5 пишет в один receive buffer, Stream3 может читать второй.
- Threshold exchange должен следовать тому же принципу: никакой in-place write/read race.

Главный bug-risk:
- Сейчас threshold update слишком привязан к dispatcher idle/drain и одному `current_threshold`.
- Нужно сделать threshold publication asynchronous-safe через double buffering и active-index commit.
- Нужно сделать histogram snapshot безопасным относительно параллельного Stream4, через существующую A/B схему или явное stable snapshot поле.

Итоговая архитектурная формула:
`Stream4 local progress -> local threshold_request -> Stream5 all-rank threshold exchange -> Stream5 writes inactive threshold buffer -> atomic active_threshold_index switch -> Stream3/Stream4 use new threshold`.
```

# Project Agent Rules

## Operating Rule
- Read `AGENTS.md` before project edits.
- Update `memory/CHANGELOG.md` after meaningful code, config, or architecture changes.
- Update `memory/PROMPTS.md` with user prompts that define requirements.
- Store test outputs, logs, and verification notes under `test_results/`.
- Prefer agent-centered code: explicit contracts, deterministic tests, small files, low hidden state.

## Architecture Source
- Primary architecture contract: `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md`.
- Current Stream 4 implementation rule: use threshold + compact + CUB/fixed-temp sort/reduce + compact; do not use Stream 4 hash-table dedup.

## Implementation Guardrails
- `State128` logical bytes are `v[0..119]`.

- Persistent frontier padding must be zero.
- `FinalResponse` may temporarily store `target_local_idx` in `v[120..123]`.
- `Hash128` is one logical 128-bit key stored as `{lo, hi}`.
- `CandidateMeta` must remain 32 bytes and 32-byte aligned.
- Stream 3 payload id must be original candidate id, not compact index.
- Stream 4 must not apply shard top-k or semantic shard cap.

    const std::uint64_t global_idx = phase_global_prefix + phase_local;
    if (global_idx >= global_keep_count) {
        return;
    }
    final_candidate_buffer[local_out] = survivor_shard[i];
}

__global__ void final_init_send_ranges_kernel(
    const std::uint32_t* final_candidate_count,
    std::uint32_t* final_request_count,
    std::uint32_t* final_send_count,
    std::uint32_t* final_send_offset,
    std::uint32_t local_rank,
    std::uint32_t world_size,
    std::uint64_t global_prefix_for_rank,
    std::uint64_t global_keep_count,
    std::uint32_t final_capacity) {
    if (blockIdx.x != 0 || threadIdx.x != 0) {
        return;
    }
    for (std::uint32_t rank = 0; rank < world_size; ++rank) {
        final_send_count[rank] = 0;
        final_send_offset[rank] = 0;
    }
    final_send_offset[world_size] = 0;
    *final_request_count = 0;
    const std::uint32_t local_keep_total = *final_candidate_count;
    if (global_keep_count == 0ULL || world_size == 0U || local_keep_total > final_capacity) {
        return;
    }
    const std::uint64_t balance_keep_count =
        world_size == 1U ? static_cast<std::uint64_t>(local_keep_total) : global_keep_count;
    const std::uint64_t local_begin = global_prefix_for_rank;
    const std::uint64_t local_end = global_prefix_for_rank + local_keep_total;
    std::uint32_t running = 0;
    final_send_offset[0] = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t rank = 0; rank < world_size; ++rank) {
        const std::uint64_t rank_begin =
            ceil_div_u64_device(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(rank) * balance_keep_count, world_size);
        const std::uint64_t rank_end =
            ceil_div_u64_device(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(rank + 1U) * balance_keep_count, world_size);
        const std::uint64_t begin = local_begin > rank_begin ? local_begin : rank_begin;
        const std::uint64_t end = local_end < rank_end ? local_end : rank_end;
        const std::uint32_t count = end > begin ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(end - begin) : 0U;
        final_send_count[rank] = count;
        running += count;
        final_send_offset[rank + 1U] = running;
    }
    *final_request_count = local_rank < world_size ? final_send_count[local_rank] : 0U;
}

__global__ void final_scatter_load_balance_kernel(
    const CandidateMeta* survivor_shard,
    const std::uint32_t* keep_flags,
    const std::uint32_t* block_offsets,
    const std::uint32_t* output_base,
    CandidateMeta* final_candidate_buffer,
    std::uint32_t* final_candidate_count,
    FinalRequest* final_request_buffer,
    std::uint32_t local_rank,
    std::uint32_t world_size,
    std::uint64_t global_prefix_for_rank,
    std::uint64_t global_keep_count,
    std::uint32_t final_capacity,
    std::uint32_t shard_count,
    std::uint32_t shard_capacity_candidates,
    std::uint32_t stream4_batch_candidates) {
    __shared__ std::uint32_t scan[256];
    const std::uint32_t tid = threadIdx.x;
    const std::uint64_t shard_capacity = shard_capacity_candidates;
    const std::uint64_t total = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(shard_count) * shard_capacity;
    const std::uint64_t i = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + tid;
    const std::uint32_t keep = i < total ? keep_flags[i] : 0U;
    scan[tid] = keep;
    __syncthreads();
    for (std::uint32_t offset = 1U; offset < blockDim.x; offset <<= 1U) {
        const std::uint32_t add = tid >= offset ? scan[tid - offset] : 0U;
        __syncthreads();
        scan[tid] += add;
        __syncthreads();
    }
    const std::uint64_t balance_keep_count =
        world_size == 1U ? static_cast<std::uint64_t>(*final_candidate_count) : global_keep_count;
    if (keep == 0U || *final_candidate_count > final_capacity || balance_keep_count == 0ULL || world_size == 0U) {
        return;
    }
    const std::uint32_t local_out = final_phase_base_device(output_base) + block_offsets[blockIdx.x] + scan[tid] - 1U;
    if (local_out >= *final_candidate_count) {
        return;
    }
    const std::uint64_t global_idx = global_prefix_for_rank + local_out;
    std::uint32_t target_rank = static_cast<std::uint32_t>((global_idx * world_size) / balance_keep_count);
    if (target_rank >= world_size) {
        target_rank = world_size - 1U;
    }
    const std::uint64_t target_rank_begin =
        ceil_div_u64_device(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(target_rank) * balance_keep_count, world_size);
    const std::uint32_t target_local_idx = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(global_idx - target_rank_begin);
    const CandidateMeta candidate = survivor_shard[i];
    final_candidate_buffer[local_out] = candidate;
    if (target_rank == local_rank) {
        FinalRequest request{};
        request.parent_idx = candidate.parent_idx;
        request.target_local_idx = target_local_idx;
        request.return_rank = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(target_rank);
        request.move = unpack_move_threshold_device(candidate.route_packed);
        final_request_buffer[target_local_idx] = request;
    }
}

        stream3_active_ring = ring;

    const auto maybe_update_threshold = [&]() -> bool {
        if (!periodic_threshold_due() || stream3_active) {

        force_periodic_threshold_update();
        return true;

        send_offset[1] = 0;

    const std::uint32_t local_i = payload_id % candidates_per_slot;

__global__ void stream3_count_owner_kernel(
    const std::uint32_t* owner_scratch,

    for (std::uint32_t stride = blockDim.x / 2; stride > 0; stride >>= 1) {

__global__ void stream3_scan_send_counts_kernel(

    }
}

__global__ void stream3_scatter_owner_kernel(
    CandidateMeta* meta_scratch,

        const std::uint32_t i = base + tid;
        const bool match = i < count && owner_scratch[i] == peer;

        scan[tid] = match ? 1U : 0U;
        __syncthreads();
        for (std::uint32_t offset = 1; offset < blockDim.x; offset <<= 1) {
            const std::uint32_t add = tid >= offset ? scan[tid - offset] : 0U;
            __syncthreads();
            scan[tid] += add;
            __syncthreads();

        if (tid == blockDim.x - 1U) {
            tile_total = scan[tid];

        __syncthreads();
        if (match) {

    }
    if (group >= groups) {

    }
    const std::uint32_t shard = unique_shard[group];
    if (shard >= shard_count) {
        return;
    }
    const std::uint32_t buffer = shard_buffer_count <= 1U ? 0U :
        (write_buffer_index[shard] % shard_buffer_count);
    const std::uint32_t physical_shard = shard * shard_buffer_count + buffer;
    const std::uint32_t raw_count = unique_counts[group];
    const std::uint32_t source_base = shard_offsets[shard];
    const std::uint32_t write_limit = shard_counts[shard];
    const std::uint32_t shard_capacity = shard_capacity_candidates;
    const std::uint32_t dirty_base = clean_count[physical_shard] + dirty_count[physical_shard];
    const std::uint32_t spill_base = spill_offsets[shard];
    const std::uint32_t active = *global_spill_active_index & 1U;
    CandidateMeta* global_spill_buffer =
        append_to_active_spill != 0U ?
        (active == 0U ? global_spill_buffer_a : global_spill_buffer_b) :

Periodic update builds the clean-survivor histogram, copies the single-GPU local histogram to the global histogram, and applies monotonic threshold initialization/update: keep `UINT32_MAX` while total survivors are below beam, then only tighten threshold.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:130:- Changed Stream 3 and Stream 4 CUDA Graph templates to read `current_threshold` from device memory at execution time instead of capturing `UINT32_MAX` at graph instantiation.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:137:- Fixed real-data depth execution issues: dispatcher now clears unused ring-slot `parent_base/count` entries each wave, and finalization resets `clean_count`, `dirty_count`, `processing_flag`, `global_spill_count[2]`, `global_spill_active_index`, `current_threshold`, and `threshold_initialized` before the next depth.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:206:- Added fixed per-shard score histogram state in `layout_streams`: `shard_score_hist_a/b`, `shard_score_hist_active_index`, and `threshold_hist_active_snapshot`. Stream4 writes a complete inactive histogram after clean compact, flips the active histogram index, and clears `processing_flag` only after the histogram is valid.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:235:- Added final-spill failure diagnostics in `cuda/dispatcher.cu`: on non-converged final Stream3 spill flush, the runner now prints per-shard clean/dirty/processing/ready counts, last Stream3 write/spill counts and offsets, active spill distribution by shard, and active-spill score min/max/average/pass/reject relative to `current_threshold`.
memory\CHANGELOG.md:237:- Added threshold filtering to Stream3 active-spill drain so spill entries above `current_threshold` do not recirculate during final spill convergence.

void check_cub(cudaError_t status, const char* op) {
    if (status != cudaSuccess) {
        throw std::runtime_error(std::string(op) + ": " + cudaGetErrorString(status));
    }
}

__global__ void stream4_mark_threshold_counts_kernel(
    const CandidateMeta* input,
    const std::uint32_t* clean_count,
    const std::uint32_t* dirty_count,
    std::uint32_t* keep_flags,
    std::uint32_t* block_counts,
    const std::uint32_t* threshold_device,
    std::uint32_t threshold_value,
    std::uint32_t capacity) {
    __shared__ std::uint32_t flags[256];
    const std::uint32_t tid = threadIdx.x;
    const std::uint32_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + tid;
    const std::uint32_t input_count = *clean_count + *dirty_count;
    const std::uint32_t threshold = threshold_device == nullptr ? threshold_value : *threshold_device;
    std::uint32_t keep = 0;
    if (i < capacity) {
        keep = i < input_count && input[i].score_key <= threshold ? 1U : 0U;
        keep_flags[i] = keep;
    }
    flags[tid] = keep;
    __syncthreads();
    for (std::uint32_t stride = blockDim.x / 2; stride > 0; stride >>= 1) {
        if (tid < stride) {
            flags[tid] += flags[tid + stride];
        }
        __syncthreads();
    }
    if (tid == 0) {
        block_counts[blockIdx.x] = flags[0];
    }
}

__global__ void stream4_scan_block_counts_kernel(
    const std::uint32_t* block_counts,

std::vector<StreamResult> benchmark_stream4(std::ofstream& report) {
    std::vector<StreamResult> results;
    report << "## Stream4 Threshold Compact Sort Reduce\n\n";
    report << "| shard_capacity | STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES | input_count | ms_per_job | shard_items_per_sec | batch_candidates_per_sec | allocation_bytes |\n";
    report << "|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n";
    for (std::uint32_t capacity : STREAM4_SHARD_CAPACITY_SWEEP) {
        std::vector<CandidateMeta> host(capacity);
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < capacity; ++i) {
            host[i].hash = Hash128{static_cast<std::uint64_t>(i), static_cast<std::uint64_t>(capacity - i)};
            host[i].parent_idx = i;
            host[i].score_key = i % SCORE_BIN_COUNT;
            host[i].route_packed = i % MOVE_COUNT;
        }
        for (std::uint32_t batch : STREAM4_BATCH_SWEEP) {
            if (batch > capacity) {
                continue;
            }

__global__ void stream5_self_count_and_offsets_kernel(
    const std::uint32_t* send_count,
    std::uint32_t* recv_count,
    std::uint32_t local_rank) {
    if (blockIdx.x == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {
        recv_count[local_rank] = send_count[local_rank];
    }
}

__global__ void stream5_self_copy_kernel(
    const CandidateMeta* remote_send_buffer,
    const std::uint32_t* send_count,
    const std::uint32_t* send_offset,
    CandidateMeta* remote_recv_buffer,
    const std::uint32_t* recv_offset,
    std::uint32_t local_rank) {
    const std::uint32_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    const std::uint32_t count = send_count[local_rank];
    if (i >= count) {
        return;
    }
    remote_recv_buffer[recv_offset[local_rank] + i] = remote_send_buffer[send_offset[local_rank] + i];
}

__global__ void stream5_self_copy_words_kernel(
    const std::uint64_t* send_buffer,
    std::uint64_t* recv_buffer,
    std::uint32_t send_offset_items,
    std::uint32_t recv_offset_items,
    std::uint32_t item_count,
    std::uint32_t words_per_item) {
    const std::uint64_t i = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    const std::uint64_t word_count = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(item_count) * words_per_item;
    if (i >= word_count) {
        return;
    }
    recv_buffer[static_cast<std::uint64_t>(recv_offset_items) * words_per_item + i] =
        send_buffer[static_cast<std::uint64_t>(send_offset_items) * words_per_item + i];
}

void stream5_exchange_counts_nccl_cuda(
    const std::uint32_t* device_send_count,
    std::uint32_t* device_recv_count,
    std::uint32_t local_rank,
    std::uint32_t world_size,
    ncclComm_t comm,
    cudaStream_t stream) {
    NvtxRange range("Stream5_NCCL_count_exchange_launch");
    if (world_size == 0 || local_rank >= world_size) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("stream5 NCCL exchange rank parameters are invalid");
    }

    check_nccl(ncclGroupStart(), "ncclGroupStart count exchange");
    for (std::uint32_t peer = 0; peer < world_size; ++peer) {
        if (peer == local_rank) {

        }
        check_nccl(ncclSend(device_send_count + peer, 1, ncclUint32, static_cast<int>(peer), comm, stream), "ncclSend send_count");
        check_nccl(ncclRecv(device_recv_count + peer, 1, ncclUint32, static_cast<int>(peer), comm, stream), "ncclRecv recv_count");
    }
    check_nccl(ncclGroupEnd(), "ncclGroupEnd count exchange");

    stream5_self_count_and_offsets_kernel<<<1, 1, 0, stream>>>(device_send_count, device_recv_count, local_rank);
}

void stream5_write_recv_offsets_cuda(
    std::uint32_t* device_recv_offset,
    const std::uint32_t* host_recv_offset,
    std::uint32_t world_size,
    cudaStream_t stream) {
    NvtxRange range("Stream5_write_recv_offsets_launch");
    cudaError_t status = cudaMemcpyAsync(
        device_recv_offset,
        host_recv_offset,
        (static_cast<std::size_t>(world_size) + 1U) * sizeof(std::uint32_t),

}

std::uint64_t parse_u64(const char* text, const char* name) {
    char* end = nullptr;
    const unsigned long long value = std::strtoull(text, &end, 10);
    if (end == text || *end != '\0') {
        throw std::invalid_argument(std::string("invalid numeric argument: ") + name);
    }
    return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(value);
}

std::uint32_t parse_next_u32(const std::string& text, std::size_t& pos, const char* context) {
    while (pos < text.size() && (text[pos] < '0' || text[pos] > '9')) {
        ++pos;
    }
    if (pos >= text.size()) {
        throw std::runtime_error(std::string("missing integer in ") + context);
    }
    std::uint64_t value = 0;
    while (pos < text.size() && text[pos] >= '0' && text[pos] <= '9') {
        value = value * 10ULL + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(text[pos] - '0');
        if (value > std::numeric_limits<std::uint8_t>::max()) {
            throw std::runtime_error(std::string("integer out of uint8 range in ") + context);
        }
        ++pos;
    }
    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(value);
}

std::string read_text_file(const std::filesystem::path& path) {
    std::ifstream file(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!file) {
        throw std::runtime_error("cannot open required text file: " + path.string());
    }
    return std::string(std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(file), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
}

std::vector<std::byte> read_binary_exact(const std::filesystem::path& path, std::size_t expected_bytes) {
    std::ifstream file(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!file) {
        throw std::runtime_error("cannot open required binary file: " + path.string());
    }
    std::vector<std::byte> bytes(expected_bytes);
    file.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));

Evidence: rank 1 depth 1 logged `request_send_counts offset1=97 offset2=209`, then `request_send_snapshot offset1=0 offset2=204`, matching `history_recv` offsets and causing corrupted `FinalRequest` payloads.
- Fixed the final exchange offset lifetime bug by adding immutable host-side `FinalExchangePlan{count, offset, total}` objects per exchange phase. `history`, `request`, and `response` now keep independent send plans, and `exchange_u64_items` builds a local receive plan per call instead of reusing caller scratch offsets.
- Tightened final exchange alignment: `FinalHistoryRecord` is now `alignas(32)` and exactly 64 bytes, `next_frontier_states_tmp` and `final_response_buffer` are allocated with at least `CandidateMeta` alignment because multi-rank final overlays them with `CandidateMeta`/`FinalHistoryRecord`, and final count/offset device service buffers are 256-byte aligned.
- Local verification after the offset-plan/alignment fix: Docker build target `production_runner` passed, targeted CUDA tests passed 5/5, and `WORLD_SIZE=1` smoke `production_runner 0 1 4194304` passed.
- Documented the three scratch-pool overlay layouts: Stream inference layout, final select/dedup layout, and final materialization layout. Layout 3 owns the static 3-slot ring for chunked GPU-GPU materialization and defines the final scratch sizing floor.
- Reworked multi-rank final materialization to chunk selected `CandidateMeta` on GPU. Requests are built from selected chunks on GPU, grouped by `source_rank`, exchanged through NCCL without CPU payload staging, materialized by source rank, regrouped by `return_rank`, and scattered into the local `next_frontier_states_tmp`. Self-source and self-return paths stay local and skip NCCL payload traffic.
- Added static layout-3 buffers: selected candidate storage, rank key ping-pong arrays, request ping-pong arrays, request receive arrays, response send/receive arrays, history send/receive arrays, and fixed CUB temp. `FinalHistoryRecord` is now a shared 64-byte/32-aligned project type.
- Replaced final exchange host control vectors in the new multi-rank final materialization path with fixed-size static arrays (`kFinalExchangeMaxWorldSize=128`) so per-chunk final request/response planning does not allocate dynamic host containers.
- Moved debug final request validation error storage from `cudaMalloc` to a static `layout_final` slot (`FinalRequestValidationError`, 48 bytes, 16-byte aligned), removing the last CUDA dynamic allocation inside final materialization code.
- Extended `static_memory_cuda_tests` with multi-rank layout-3 capacity/alignment assertions for 3 slots, exchange capacity, selected-buffer sizing, request/response/history slot pointers, and 256-byte CUB temp alignment.
- Local verification after layout-3 materialization changes: Docker full build passed, targeted CUDA tests passed 4/4 (`final_cuda_tests`, `threshold_cuda_tests`, `dispatcher_cuda_tests`, `static_memory_cuda_tests`), and a manual small-config `WORLD_SIZE=1` `production_runner 0 1 4096` smoke passed. Local default auto-config smoke still fails on the RTX 3070 Laptop GPU budget, so real multi-rank runtime validation remains pending on Kaggle T4x2. Report saved as `test_results/final_materialize_layout3_2026-05-26.md`.
- Reduced multi-rank final materialization static memory: full `final_request_buffer[N_LOCAL]` is now allocated only for `WORLD_SIZE=1`, full `final_response_buffer` is omitted for `WORLD_SIZE>1`, and the multi-rank selected-candidate buffer is capped at `min(GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_EFFECTIVE, survivor_count)` instead of using the whole `State128` frontier byte area.
- Added layout-3 slot events for multi-rank final materialization: `build_done`, `history_done`, `request_done`, `response_ready`, and `response_done`. Final request/history/response exchanges now record payload completion events, and response receive scatter is deferred until slot drain so response NCCL transfer can overlap later chunk work.
- Kept the final exchange receive-offset host-to-device copy synchronous before payload enqueue so async payload execution never references stack-backed receive offset arrays after the exchange helper returns.
- Updated `static_memory_cuda_tests` expectations for the reduced multi-rank layout: full request/response buffers must be absent in multi-rank final materialization, while 3-slot request/response/history buffers and fixed CUB temp remain statically allocated and aligned.
- Prepared the Kaggle T4x2 validation path to use GitHub `main` as the source of truth rather than a source-archive dataset. The notebook diagnostic depth is set to 8 for a short multi-rank final-materialization test.
- Diagnosed the next Kaggle T4x2 failure from user-provided logs: final materialization progressed past the previous exchange corruption, then rank 1 failed during depth 6 `stream3_remote_recv_collect` with fatal code `3002` (`STREAM_FATAL_STREAM3_DOUBLE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW`). No code was changed during this diagnostic pass. The observed state was physical shard 7 processing with `clean=3988985`, `dirty=146907`, `existing=4135892`, `available=0`, `raw_count=24057`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY=0`; likely design gaps are missing remote-receive backpressure and disabled synchronized periodic threshold updates for multi-rank depth flow.
- Added diagnostic-only fatal trace fields for Stream3 double-buffer overflow: logical shard, selected buffer, sibling physical shard, sibling clean/dirty/processing counts, sibling existing/available capacity, and shard buffer count. No scheduling or backpressure behavior changed.
- Enabled all existing Kaggle diagnostic logging switches for the next T4x2 run: Stream timing, inference trace, path trace, final validation, final exchange trace, depth logs, debug logs, live rank logs, and runtime `BEAM_DEBUG_PIPELINE_STATS`.
- Kaggle version 54 reproduced Stream3 fatal code `3002` with expanded diagnostics: both ranks failed in `stream3_remote_recv_collect` at depth 6 after both physical buffers for the target logical shard became `processing=1`. Rank 0 failed on logical shard 2 (`selected=4`, sibling `5`) and rank 1 failed on logical shard 3 (`selected=7`, sibling `6`). Current leading hypothesis: Stream4 can start processing a physical shard that Stream3 previously counted as the writable buffer while a Stream3 ring is still in flight; the local writable-buffer check is not a reservation, and remote receive has no independent ingress reserve. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v54_stream3_diagnostics_2026-05-26.md`.
- Fixed the Stream4 ready-queue A/B scheduling invariant. `stream3_build_ready_shard_queue_kernel` now builds readiness per logical shard, skips any logical shard with an active Stream4 physical buffer, emits at most one physical buffer per logical shard, prioritizes dirty-ready buffers over clean-only buffers during forced flush, and updates `stream3_write_buffer_index` to a non-processing sibling when one has capacity. Added Stream3 CUDA regression tests for logical-shard mutual exclusion, busy-sibling skip, and dirty-priority final flush. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with the logical/physical shard contract: Stream3 is the only Stream4 buffer writer, Stream5 only fills `remote_recv_buffer`, and Stream4 may process at most one A/B physical buffer per logical shard at a time.
- Disabled Stream3 pre-launch writable-buffer backpressure for multi-rank execution. The dispatcher now keeps the backpressure ready-queue drain only when `WORLD_SIZE == 1`; when `WORLD_SIZE > 1`, Stream3 launches normally and any lack of A/B write capacity remains an explicit fatal overflow instead of being hidden by scheduler throttling. Updated `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md` with this single-GPU-only backpressure rule.
- Kaggle version 55 confirmed the A/B logical-shard mutex fix changed the failure mode: neither rank had both A/B buffers processing for the failed logical shard. Rank 1 failed with selected physical shard 0 non-processing but nearly full (`existing=4176369`, `available=17935`, `raw_count=24033`) while sibling physical shard 1 was processing; rank 0 failed similarly on logical shard 3. The revealed issue is multi-rank capacity saturation because periodic threshold updates were disabled for `WORLD_SIZE>1`, causing per-rank clean totals around 31M before depth 6 drained.
- Enabled periodic threshold updates for multi-rank without cross-rank synchronization. Periodic multi-rank updates now build a local completed-shard histogram and update `current_threshold` from that local histogram only; final global threshold still uses NCCL/global aggregation after local final flush.
- Softened the remaining single-GPU double-buffer backpressure path: if the writable-buffer reserve check fails but no ready Stream4 work exists, the dispatcher logs `stream3_backpressure_bypass` and launches Stream3 instead of throwing a scheduler error. Multi-rank execution still bypasses this pre-launch backpressure entirely.
- Kaggle version 57 diagnostic run on T4x2 failed with `code=3002` after depth 5. Stream timings show depth 5 wall time about `2.95s`, Stream4 cumulative time about `3.12-3.18s` across two slots, Stream3 ring time about `1.94s`, Stream1/2 time about `1.13s`, and Stream5 time about `0.38s`. Buffer diagnostics show both ranks near `32M` clean resident candidates and `threshold_updates_depth=0` before fatal. Failure occurs during `stream3_remote_recv_collect` before the scheduler gets a chance to update threshold, so the current issue is threshold scheduling/pruning timing rather than the old A/B mutex bug. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v57_stream_timing_buffers_2026-05-26.md`.

## 2026-05-26 Stream5 threshold update contract

```text
WORLD_SIZE == 1:
    threshold scheduling may keep the existing single-GPU host-side periodic path.

WORLD_SIZE > 1:
    GLOBAL_THRESHOLD_UPDATE_PERIOD_SHARDS must not drive threshold scheduling.
    Stream4 remains local and does not call NCCL.
    Stream4 histogram publication remains per-shard A/B:
        Stream4 writes inactive shard_score_hist buffer.
        Stream4 commits shard_score_hist_active_index only after inactive histogram is complete.
        Stream5 threshold snapshot reads shard_score_hist_active_index, then sums the selected A/B buffers.
    Stream5 owns threshold collective communication.
    Each rank publishes threshold_request_local as a service field after enough completed local Stream4 work.
    Every rank participates in threshold request reduction at Stream5 exchange points.
    Collective request reduction:
        threshold_request_global = ncclAllReduceMax(threshold_request_local)
    If threshold_request_global != 0:
        every rank builds local_score_hist from committed Stream4 histogram A/B buffers.
        every rank participates in NCCL SUM local_score_hist -> global_score_hist.
        every rank computes monotonic current_threshold.
        every rank resets its local processed-work threshold counter.

current_threshold publication:
    current_threshold has two slots.
    threshold_initialized has two slots.
    current_threshold_active_index selects the committed slot.
    Stream5 writes inactive current_threshold slot first.
    Stream5 writes inactive threshold_initialized slot second.
    Stream5 commits current_threshold_active_index after device memory fence.
    Stream3 reads current_threshold[current_threshold_active_index & 1].
    Stream4 reads current_threshold[current_threshold_active_index & 1].
    No new atomic operations are allowed in threshold publication or request fields.
```
```text
STATE_LEN = 120
STATE_STORAGE_LEN = 128
STATE_VALUE_PAD = 128

SCORE_MAX_Q = 300.0
SCORE_SCALE = 1024
SCORE_MAX_KEY = SCORE_MAX_Q * SCORE_SCALE
SCORE_BIN_COUNT = SCORE_MAX_KEY + 1
GOAL_SCORE_KEY = 0

RING_SLOT_COUNT =
    STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES / (B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT)

STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES =
    RING_SLOT_COUNT * B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT

-- Replaced the previous multi-rank local-only periodic threshold update with a Stream5-owned collective request/update path. Multi-rank dispatch now reflects completed local Stream4 work into `threshold_request_local`, all ranks run an `ncclAllReduce(Max)` request check at Stream5 exchange points, and any rank request triggers a global histogram allreduce plus monotonic threshold update on all ranks before remote receive collection. Added double-buffered `current_threshold[2]`, `threshold_initialized[2]`, and `current_threshold_active_index`; Stream5 writes the inactive slot and commits by active-index update after a device fence, while Stream3/Stream4 read only the committed slot. +- Replaced the previous multi-rank local-only periodic threshold update with a Stream5-owned collective request/update path. Multi-rank dispatch now reflects completed local Stream4 work into `threshold_request_local`, all ranks run an `ncclAllReduce(Max)` request check at Stream5 exchange points, and any rank request triggers a global histogram allreduce plus monotonic threshold update on all ranks before remote receive collection. The dispatcher refreshes completed Stream4 slots immediately before the Stream5 request check so jobs that finish while waiting for Stream3 are counted. __global__ void validate_final_requests_kernel(
    const FinalRequest* requests,
    FinalRequestValidationError* error,
    std::uint32_t request_count,
    std::uint64_t current_frontier_size,
    std::uint32_t target_count) {
    const std::uint32_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (i >= request_count) {
        return;
    }
    const FinalRequest request = requests[i];
    std::uint32_t reason = 0;
    if (request.parent_idx >= current_frontier_size) {
        reason |= FinalRequestInvalidParent;
    }
    if (request.target_local_idx >= target_count) {
        reason |= FinalRequestInvalidTarget;
    }
    if (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(request.move) >= MOVE_COUNT) {
        reason |= FinalRequestInvalidMove;
    }
    if (request.target_local_idx != i) {
        reason |= FinalRequestInvalidSlot;
    }
    if (reason == 0U) {
        return;
    }

    atomicAdd(&error->invalid_count, 1U);
    if (atomicCAS(&error->first_index, UINT32_MAX, i) == UINT32_MAX) {
        error->parent_idx = request.parent_idx;
        error->target_local_idx = request.target_local_idx;
        error->request_count = request_count;
        error->current_frontier_size = current_frontier_size;
        error->target_count = target_count;
        error->reason_mask = reason;
        error->move = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(request.move);
    }
}
#endif

    response.v[121] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(target_local_idx >> 8);
    response.v[122] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(target_local_idx >> 16);
    response.v[123] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(target_local_idx >> 24);
}

    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(response.v[120]) |
           (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(response.v[121]) << 8) |
           (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(response.v[122]) << 16) |
           (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(response.v[123]) << 24);
}

}

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: D:\100XH100\memory\CHANGELOG.md

-- Replaced the previous multi-rank local-only periodic threshold update with a Stream5-owned collective request/update path. Multi-rank dispatch now reflects completed local Stream4 work into `threshold_request_local`, all ranks run an `ncclAllReduce(Max)` request check at Stream5 exchange points, and any rank request triggers a global histogram allreduce plus monotonic threshold update on all ranks before remote receive collection. The dispatcher refreshes completed Stream4 slots immediately before the Stream5 request check so jobs that finish while waiting for Stream3 are counted. Added double-buffered `current_threshold[2]`, `threshold_initialized[2]`, and `current_threshold_active_index`; Stream5 writes the inactive slot and commits by active-index update after a device fence, while Stream3/Stream4 read only the committed slot. Added service fields `threshold_request_local/global`; no new atomics were introduced. Docker verification: `production_runner` build passed; `threshold_cuda_tests`, `static_memory_cuda_tests`, and `dispatcher_cuda_tests` passed. Local `production_runner 0 8 1048576` and `0 8 262144` could not run on the current GPU because runtime config fitting failed with `budget=6658457600`, `free_before=7463763968`, `headroom=805306368`. +- Replaced the previous multi-rank local-only periodic threshold update with a Stream5-owned collective request/update path. Multi-rank dispatch now reflects completed local Stream4 work into `threshold_request_local`, all ranks run an `ncclAllReduce(Max)` request check at Stream5 exchange points, and any rank request triggers a global histogram allreduce plus monotonic threshold update on all ranks before remote receive collection. The dispatcher refreshes completed Stream4 slots immediately before the Stream5 request check so jobs that finish while waiting for Stream3 are counted. Added double-buffered `current_threshold[2]`, `threshold_initialized[2]`, and `current_threshold_active_index`; Stream5 writes the inactive slot and commits by active-index update after a device fence, while Stream3/Stream4 read only the committed slot. Added service fields `threshold_request_local/global`; no new atomics were introduced. Removed debug-only atomics from final request validation, leaving atomics only in Stream2. Docker verification: release `production_runner` build passed; full diagnostic `production_runner` build with `BEAM_DEBUG_FINAL_VALIDATE=ON` passed; `threshold_cuda_tests`, `static_memory_cuda_tests`, and `dispatcher_cuda_tests` passed. Local `production_runner 0 8 1048576` and `0 8 262144` could not run on the current GPU because runtime config fitting failed with `budget=6658457600`, `free_before=7463763968`, `headroom=805306368`. Verification note saved as `test_results/threshold_stream5_collective_verification_2026-05-26.md`.
*** End Patch

```

Exit code: 0

- Removed the uncommitted Stream3 spill backpressure code from `cuda/dispatcher.cu` at user request. The current confirmed defect remains diagnostic-only: Kaggle version 26 showed a tracked candidate dropped because active global spill was full (`spill_idx=22544695`, `spill_capacity=16908288`, `spill_capacity_drop=1`). Any implementation fix must be discussed before code changes.
- Added a Stream3/Stream4 config-search derivation model. `GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH_MAX_SAFE` was removed; effective beam width is now only `round_up(USER_GLOBAL_BEAM_WIDTH, WORLD_SIZE * SHARD_COUNT * STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES_PER_SHARD_UNIT)`. `STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES` is derived from `BEAM_STREAM3_RING_SLOTS * B_MICRO * MOVE_COUNT`, `RING_COUNT` is derived from logical shard size, and `SHARD_COUNT/STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES` are selected under `layout_streams_bytes <= layout_final_budget_bytes` and GPU memory budget.
- Added `StaticMemoryPlan.layout_final_budget_bytes` so production config search can compare stream-layout memory against the final-stage budget without using the previous self-expanding `layout_final_bytes` value.
- Kaggle version 28 verified the config-search build on T4 but failed fast through the existing Stream3 spill fatal guard. The selected config used `STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES=1398784` and `GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY=393216`; shard 3 was still `processing_flag=1`, active spill was already `388323/393216`, and a new `32593`-candidate spill group exceeded capacity. Report saved as `test_results/kaggle_v28_config_search_spill_guard_2026-05-24.md`.
- Updated the production config-search objective after the Kaggle v28 spill guard failure. Default spill capacity now uses the architecture backlog bound `max(2*STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES, STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS*LOGICAL_SHARD_SIZE)`, and candidate scoring now balances Stream4 waves, Stream4 jobs, Stream4 batch units, jobs per logical shard, and shards per sort slot. Added knobs `BEAM_MIN_STREAM4_JOBS_PER_SHARD`, `BEAM_TARGET_STREAM4_JOBS_PER_SHARD`, and `BEAM_TARGET_SHARDS_PER_SORT_SLOT`.
- Kaggle version 29 caught an NVCC-only compile issue in the new spill bound expression: `std::max` received mixed `unsigned long long` and `unsigned long` operands. Fixed the expression by materializing the concurrent shard backlog as `std::uint64_t`.
- Kaggle version 30 showed the same NVCC deduction issue remained because `2ULL` still forced `unsigned long long`; the spill bound expression now uses `std::max<std::uint64_t>` explicitly.
- Kaggle version 31 built successfully and exposed a resident-window flow problem: `SHARD_COUNT=7`, `STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES=799744`, and `N_LOCAL=16780288`; Stream3 hit the fatal guard when shard 1 reached `clean_count=1599488 == 2*STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES`. The rejected invariant `SHARD_COUNT*2*STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES >= N_LOCAL` is intentionally not in code because resident Stream4 shard storage is a processing window, not full logical-shard storage. The remaining fix must address scheduler/threshold/backlog flow.
- Decoupled resident shard capacity from Stream4 batch sizing. `RuntimeConfig` now has `SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES`, `SHARD_CAPACITY_SCALE_PPM`, `STREAM4_BATCH_ALIGNMENT`, and `GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`; `survivor_shard` is allocated as `SHARD_COUNT * SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES`, while Stream4 batch remains the dirty-count launch threshold. Production config search derives shard capacity from `LOGICAL_SHARD_SIZE * SHARD_CAPACITY_SCALE_PPM` and derives default spill as `STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES * GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`.
- Kaggle version 32 compiled but stopped on explicit Stream3 spill-capacity fatal at depth 5 (`spill_end=1584778`, `spill_capacity=1572864`). Default spill derivation now includes the Stream4 worker multiplier: `STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS * STREAM3_BATCH_CANDIDATES * GLOBAL_SPILL_SCALE_PPM`.
- Added per-depth stream timing diagnostics. `depth_done` now logs Stream1/2 ring graph time, Stream3 ring time, Stream3 final spill-drain time, final filter/materialize/reset time, Stream4 job time/avg/max, Stream5 threshold time, Stream4 queue peaks, and global spill peak.
- Added master debug gating. `BEAM_ENABLE_DEBUG=OFF` now forces depth logs, general debug logs, stream timing, inference trace, and path trace off at compile time.         check_cuda(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&streams.stream4_slot_streams[slot], cudaStreamNonBlocking), "cudaStreamCreate stream4 slot");
        check_cuda(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&streams.stream4_slot_done[slot], cudaEventDisableTiming), "cudaEventCreate stream4 slot done");
    }
}

void ensure_final_slot_events(DispatcherStreams& streams) {
    auto create_group = [](std::array<cudaEvent_t, 3>& events, const char* label) {
        for (std::uint32_t slot = 0; slot < events.size(); ++slot) {
            if (events[slot] == nullptr) {
                check_cuda(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&events[slot], cudaEventDisableTiming), label);
            }
        }
    };
    create_group(streams.final_build_done, "cudaEventCreate final build done");
    create_group(streams.final_history_done, "cudaEventCreate final history done");
    create_group(streams.final_request_done, "cudaEventCreate final request done");
    create_group(streams.final_response_ready, "cudaEventCreate final response ready");
    create_group(streams.final_response_done, "cudaEventCreate final response done");
}

void update_threshold_global(
    const StaticMemoryPlan& plan,
    StaticDeviceMemory& memory,
    cudaStream_t stream,
    bool periodic,
    const DispatcherCollective* collective,
    bool local_histogram_only = false) {
    const std::uint64_t threshold_width = plan.derived.global_beam_width_effective;
    threshold_build_local_histogram_cuda(
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_a,
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_b,
        memory.streams.shard_score_hist_active_index,
        memory.streams.threshold_hist_active_snapshot,
        memory.streams.local_score_hist,
        plan.storage_shard_count,
        stream);
    if (plan.config.world_size == 1U || local_histogram_only) {
        check_cuda(cudaMemcpyAsync(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.local_score_hist,
            SCORE_BIN_COUNT * sizeof(std::uint64_t),
            cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice,
            stream), "cudaMemcpyAsync single gpu histogram");
    } else {
        if (collective == nullptr || collective->comm == nullptr) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("multi rank threshold update requires NCCL collective");
        }
        threshold_allreduce_histogram_nccl_cuda(
            memory.streams.local_score_hist,
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            collective->comm,
            stream);
    }
    if (periodic) {
        threshold_update_periodic_cuda(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.current_threshold,
            memory.streams.threshold_initialized,
            memory.streams.current_threshold_active_index,
            threshold_width,
            stream);
    } else {
        threshold_select_cuda(
            memory.streams.global_score_hist,
            memory.streams.current_threshold,
            memory.streams.threshold_initialized,
            memory.streams.current_threshold_active_index,
            threshold_width,
            stream);
    }
}

std::uint32_t read_committed_threshold_host(const StaticDeviceMemory& memory, const char* op) {

        memory.streams.current_threshold + (active & 1U),
        sizeof(threshold),
        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), op);
    return threshold;
}

## 1440. Codex

Time: `2026-05-26T19:27:28.020Z` · source line `2336`

```text
Главная причина: это был full-debug ран, не performance-run.

Факторы торможения:
- Kaggle build сам занял ~108s: clone + CMake + CUDA build.
- `BEAM_DEBUG_PIPELINE_STATS=1` очень дорогой: почти каждый scheduler event делает GPU→CPU копии `clean/dirty/processing/spill` и печатает `pipeline_stats/pipeline_shards`.
- `BEAM_DEBUG_FINAL_EXCHANGE_TRACE=ON` спамит final exchange; на больших depth это тысячи строк.
- live rank logging через Python pipe/Kaggle UI может реально блокировать C++ stdout.
- `BEAM_DEBUG_STREAM_TIMING=ON` добавляет event timing и sync points.
- новый Stream5 threshold update добавляет NCCL histogram allreduce: `307201 * uint64 ~= 2.46MB` на update, плюс синхронизация Stream5. Это ожидаемый overhead, но не должен быть production-режимом.

По v58 видно: compute не выглядел катастрофически медленным до cancel. Depth 1-4 были ~0.24s, `depth4=0.319s`; depth5 дошел до Stream4/final drain, но `depth_done=5` не успел записаться. То есть “медленно” в основном из-за debug/logging/build/cancel, а не из-за явной деградации ядра.

Для следующего замера скорости надо оставить только:
`BEAM_ENABLE_DEPTH_LOGS=ON`, `BEAM_DEBUG_STREAM_TIMING=ON`, `BEAM_DEBUG_PIPELINE_STATS=0`, `BEAM_DEBUG_FINAL_EXCHANGE_TRACE=OFF`, path/inference trace off. Тогда будет нормальная картина по Stream1/3/4/5.
```

namespace beam {

void check_cuda(cudaError_t status, const char* op) {
    if (status != cudaSuccess) {
        throw std::runtime_error(std::string(op) + ": " + cudaGetErrorString(status));
    }
}

void check_nccl_dispatcher(ncclResult_t status, const char* op) {
    if (status != ncclSuccess) {
        throw std::runtime_error(std::string(op) + ": " + ncclGetErrorString(status));
    }
}

constexpr std::uint32_t kFinalExchangeMaxWorldSize = 128;

struct alignas(64) FinalExchangePlan {
    std::array<std::uint32_t, kFinalExchangeMaxWorldSize> count{};
    std::array<std::uint32_t, kFinalExchangeMaxWorldSize + 1U> offset{};
    std::uint32_t size = 0;
    std::uint32_t total = 0;
};

static_assert(alignof(FinalExchangePlan) == 64);

FinalExchangePlan make_final_exchange_plan(const std::uint32_t* counts, std::uint32_t count_size) {
    if (count_size > kFinalExchangeMaxWorldSize) {
        throw std::runtime_error("final exchange world size exceeds static control capacity");
    }
    FinalExchangePlan plan{};
    plan.size = count_size;
    std::uint64_t running = 0;
    plan.offset[0] = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < count_size; ++i) {
        plan.count[i] = counts[i];
        running += counts[i];
        if (running > static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max())) {
            throw std::runtime_error("exchange item count exceeds uint32 range");
        }
        plan.offset[i + 1U] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(running);
    }
    plan.total = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(running);
    return plan;
}

#if BEAM_DEBUG_STREAM_TIMING
void accumulate_elapsed_ms(
    cudaEvent_t start,
    cudaEvent_t stop,
    double& total_ms,
    double* max_ms,
    const char* op) {
    float elapsed_ms = 0.0f;
    check_cuda(cudaEventElapsedTime(&elapsed_ms, start, stop), op);
    total_ms += static_cast<double>(elapsed_ms);
    if (max_ms != nullptr) {
        *max_ms = std::max(*max_ms, static_cast<double>(elapsed_ms));
    }
}
#endif

#if BEAM_DEBUG_FINAL_EXCHANGE_TRACE
void log_final_exchange_counts(

        std::cout << " offset" << i << "=" << plan.offset[i];

void threshold_build_local_histogram_cuda(
    const std::uint32_t* shard_score_hist_a,
    const std::uint32_t* shard_score_hist_b,
    const std::uint32_t* shard_score_hist_active_index,
    std::uint32_t* threshold_hist_active_snapshot,
    std::uint64_t* local_score_hist,
    std::uint32_t shard_count,
    cudaStream_t stream) {
    NvtxRange range("Threshold_sum_shard_histograms_launch");
    const std::uint32_t block_size = 256;
    const dim3 block(block_size);
    const dim3 shard_grid((shard_count + block_size - 1U) / block_size);
    const dim3 hist_grid((SCORE_BIN_COUNT + block_size - 1U) / block_size);
    threshold_snapshot_active_histogram_kernel<<<shard_grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
        shard_score_hist_active_index,
        threshold_hist_active_snapshot,
        shard_count);
    threshold_sum_shard_histograms_kernel<<<hist_grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
        shard_score_hist_a,
        shard_score_hist_b,
        threshold_hist_active_snapshot,
        local_score_hist,
        shard_count);
}

void threshold_select_cuda(

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: D:\100XH100\memory\PROMPTS.md
@@
 - User finalized the threshold architecture: no new atomic operations are allowed; only Stream2 may use atomics. Threshold publication must be async-safe via double-buffered `current_threshold` plus active-index commit. Histogram snapshot must remain safe against parallel Stream4 through the existing per-shard histogram A/B scheme. Stream4/Stream3/Stream1/Stream2 remain local; Stream5 owns inter-rank communication. Stream4 exposes a local threshold request signal after enough processed work, Stream5 sees the signal, all ranks participate in the collective threshold update, the triggering and participating ranks reset their local counters, and `GLOBAL_THRESHOLD_UPDATE_PERIOD_SHARDS` must not drive multi-rank threshold scheduling.
+- User observed that Kaggle version 58 looked hung because logs stopped around 122 seconds while the run stayed active past 300 seconds, then requested detailed non-spam diagnostics for the 2xT4 run to identify the stall point.
*** End Patch

```

In this diagnostic build only, the trace adds stream synchronizations after local histogram, NCCL histogram, and threshold publish so a silent stall can be localized to the exact stage. Все агенты обязаны использовать строго эксплицитный, буквальный, низко-амбигуозный и высокоплотный стиль коммуникации (AML-HIP). Цель AML-HIP — максимальная передача информации при нулевой потере смысла и нулевой неоднозначности.

ОСНОВНЫЕ ПРИНЦИПЫ:

1. Максимальная плотность информации на строку.
